text:
kevin: heads-up — i'm prototyping a grafana dashboard to catch sub-minute GPU microbursts that cause thermal throttles and pstate drops. quick sanity-check on queries/panels before i land it?

maria: :eyes: nice. are you correlating power draw + fan rpm + nvlink/pcie errors? those are good early indicators.

kevin: yes. planned panels: 1) 30s rolling max gpu utilization (per-gpu), 2) short-window memory alloc churn (event count), 3) inlet temp + fan rpm, 4) power draw + pstate transitions, 5) nvlink/rdma error spikes, plus a compact sparkline for allocation op tail latency.

raj: can you paste the promql for the 30s window? we sample at 15s so window math matters.

kevin: draft queries:```
# 30s max util per GPU
max_over_time(node_gpu_utilization_percent{job="gpu_exporter"}[30s])

# memory alloc churn (event counter)
increase(nvidia_mem_alloc_events_total[30s])

# fan rpm (1m avg)
avg_over_time(node_gpu_fan_rpm{job="gpu_exporter"}[1m])
```

maria: for counters use increase(), good. also consider histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(...)) if we have request latency histograms.

kevin: switched churn to increase(nvidia_mem_alloc_events_total[30s]). thanks.

alyssa: UI asks: add dashboard variables for $region and $rack, toggle for per-gpu vs per-node rollup, and a collapsed lane showing only GPUs currently spiking (topk(10, ...)).

kevin: adding $region, $rack, $node, $gpu_index. will add a compact active-gpus lane using topk.

sre-oncall: alerting suggestion: avoid firing on single short spikes. create recording rules to aggregate bursts over 5m, then page only if sustained and affecting multiple GPUs or >1% of fleet. example alert:```
- alert: GPU_Microburst_Cluster
  expr: sum(increase(gpu_microburst_events_total[5m])) > 100
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwoodinternal/runbooks/gpu-microburst
```

kevin: we'll do that. also building a composite panel that overlays inlet temp vs temp delta over 10m to show hysteresis and delayed throttles.

raj: add derived "throttle_latency": time between usage/power spike and first pstate drop. approx with timestamp() and last_over_time tricks; noisy but useful as a trend.

maria: for visuals use grafana transforms to compute ratios and apply color thresholds: green <60% burst, yellow 60-80, red >80. top row should be a concise sparkline + threshold for quick on-call triage.

kevin: another panel idea: slot headroom forecast that extrapolates minutes-of-headroom based on current slot allocation rate. promql sketch:```
slot_alloc_rate = rate(gpu_slot_allocations_total[1m])
headroom_min = (allocatable_gpus - used_gpus) / slot_alloc_rate
```
we can't compute allocatable easily in promql arithmetic across multiple series, so i'll surface allocatable/used and let grafana math do it.

alyssa: add links from panels to Loki filtered logs for node/gpu labels, e.g. loki/query?query={node="$node",gpu="$gpu_index"} |= "OOM" — so on-call can jump straight to relevant logs.

kevin: will add panel links to logs and to the gpu-ops playbook + throttling runbook. also will ensure every PR includes dashboard UID and short summary per ops-bot reminder.

sre-oncall: to reduce noise, suppress alerts during maintenance windows and when cluster_autoscaler_scale_up is active. we had a pager storm during last rebalancing.

maria: add a tiny text panel with quick mitigations: increase burst headroom (reserve slots), enable KV prefix caching, move low-priority jobs to preemptible capacity, or tune pod eviction.

kevin: good. i'll put dashboard JSON in infra repo at dashboards/gpu/microburst-thermal.json and add an infra-ci test that verifies variables exist and that at least one panel links to runbook.

raj: :thumbsup: also include host NIC queue drops and pci error panels — microbursts can coincide with IO backpressure.

kevin: adding node_network_receive_drop_total and pci_error_count panels. i'll push a draft by EOD for review. ping @maria @raj @alyssa if you want to be reviewers.

ops-bot: reminder: grafana change requests must include dashboard UID and a short summary. use label team=eng-infra on the PR.

maria: i'll review once it's up. thanks kevin!
